Per-Group Cohort Eligibility Summary (One Report, Every Eligibility Fact)

Source: R/profile_eligibility.R
profile_summarize_cohort_eligibility.Rd

Assembles, in one call, the single per-group eligibility report a pipeline review actually wants to read: event/patient counts, the complete/partial/zero-observed breakdown, BOTH independent eligibility verdicts this family computes, and the full class/pair/higher-order support tables – instead of a caller re-deriving this by hand from five separate calls. This is purely a REPORTING layer: it calls profile_audit_support, profile_audit_interaction_support, profile_plan_precision, profile_define_cohort, and profile_precision_bound once each, on the SAME already-cohort-filtered data – it computes nothing new beyond assembling their outputs into one table.

Usage

profile_summarize_cohort_eligibility(
  data,
  group_col,
  panel,
  class_col = NULL,
  value_col = "antibiotic_value",
  resistant_values = c("R", "Resistant", "resistant"),
  susceptible_values = c("S", "Susceptible", "susceptible"),
  intermediate_values = c("I", "Intermediate", "intermediate"),
  intermediate_as_resistant = TRUE,
  event_id_col,
  patient_id_col = NULL,
  epsilon,
  alpha = 0.05,
  tiers = c(tier1 = 5, tier2 = 7.5, tier3 = 10),
  min_tier = "tier2",
  estimands = c("class", "pair", "profile"),
  conf_level = 0.95,
  max_interaction_order = NULL,
  min_co_tested = 5L,
  unknown_action = c("error", "treat_as_untested"),
  conflict_action = c("error", "drop_conflicts", "resistant_wins", "susceptible_wins",
    "first")
)

Arguments

data

Data frame, already restricted to the modeling cohort (e.g. profile_select_cohort(...)$data) – every count here describes THIS cohort, never the full unfiltered dataset.

group_col, class_col, value_col, resistant_values, susceptible_values, intermediate_values, intermediate_as_resistant, unknown_action, conflict_action

Same meaning as in profile_audit_support.

panel

Character vector. The candidate panel's classes (what profile_check_panel_feasibility calls one entry of candidate_panels, and profile_prepare_model_data calls panel).

event_id_col

Character. Required (no default, unlike elsewhere in this family) – event counting is this function's whole job, and a fallback row-index id would silently miscount events for long-format data (one row per class per event, not one row per event).

patient_id_col

Character or NULL. Column identifying the patient. When supplied, n_patients is the count of DISTINCT patients per group; when NULL (default), n_patients is NA_integer_ – no other function in this family tracks patient identity, so it is never inferred from something else.

epsilon

Numeric in (0,1). Passed to profile_precision_bound for direct_support_pass.

alpha

Numeric in (0,1). Passed to profile_precision_bound. Default 0.05.

tiers, min_tier, estimands, conf_level

Passed to profile_plan_precision/profile_define_cohort for included_in_fit. Defaults match those functions' own defaults.

max_interaction_order

Integer or NULL. Passed to profile_audit_interaction_support as max_order. Ignored (that table is returned empty) when length(panel) < 2.

min_co_tested

Integer. Passed to profile_audit_interaction_support. Default 5L.

Value

A list:

summary

one row per group: group, n_pathogen_events, n_patients, n_complete, n_partial, n_zero_observed, direct_support_pass, included_in_fit

class

profile_audit_support's $class table, on this cohort/panel

pair

profile_audit_support's $pair table, on this cohort/panel

interaction

profile_audit_interaction_support's table (higher-order support); empty data frame if length(panel) < 2

Details

The two eligibility verdicts are genuinely independent, not duplicates of each other – see profile_precision_bound's docs for why neither subsumes the other:

direct_support_pass

this group's n_complete meets profile_precision_bound's distribution-free, Hoeffding/union-bound n_min for this exact panel.

included_in_fit

this group clears min_tier on every requested estimand, per the Wilson/Goodman precision-tier roster decision in profile_define_cohort.

A group can pass one and fail the other.

n_zero_observed needs care: the shared pivot this family uses internally only produces a row for events with AT LEAST ONE tested panel class, so a naive count over that pivot would silently miss zero-observed events entirely rather than counting them. This function reconstructs the full event universe from data itself (via group_col + event_id_col) and left-joins the tested-class counts onto it, so an event with nothing tested on this panel is correctly tallied as n_zero_observed, not silently dropped.
